The test image shows a black garbage bag filled with dried, completely desiccated corn leaves — uniformly tan/brown and papery. No green tissue, no obvious fungal structures or pustules visible. The material appears to be collected dried leaf samples.

Key visual features:
- Long, narrow dried corn leaf blades
- Uniformly tan to light brown/gray coloration
- Papery, brittle texture
- No visible pustules, galls, black dots, or distinct lesion patterns

The uniform tan-gray drying of entire leaves matches **Northern Corn Leaf Blight** in its severe, late stage — the description notes "lesions spread to all leafy structures" causing them to become "grayish-green and brittle, resembling leaves killed by frost." The grayish-tan coloration of the dried blades aligns with this.

The reference image for NCLB shows cigar-shaped gray-tan lesions that, when severe, would destroy entire leaves leaving this type of uniformly dried tan/gray material.
